itineraries_found.summary: An adventure-focused 7-day itinerary starting with 2 days in Old San Juan, Day 3 in El Yunque, Day 4 at Playa Las Golondrias, and Days 5-7 in Rincon with a Crash Boat Beach finale.

venues_mentioned.name: Castillo San Cristóbal
venues_mentioned.context: Visit first thing in the morning to avoid cruise ship crowds; $10, free with America the Beautiful Pass

venues_mentioned.name: La Casa Estrecha (smallest house)
venues_mentioned.context: Schedule via Instagram @lacasaestrecha

venues_mentioned.name: Limbers de San Juan
venues_mentioned.context: Shaved ice stand; $1; perfect for a hot day

venues_mentioned.name: Barrachina
venues_mentioned.context: Where the Piña Colada was (allegedly) invented; felt pretty touristy

venues_mentioned.name: Casita Miramar
venues_mentioned.context: Alcapurrias, mofongo, canoa de ropa vieja; house hot sauce Che Che Colè; worth the drive

venues_mentioned.name: Princesa
venues_mentioned.context: Beautiful and perfect for a romantic date; standout bread pudding dessert

venues_mentioned.name: Mercado La Carreta
venues_mentioned.context: Cute brunch spot with a lot of options; Cuban sandwich, French toast

venues_mentioned.name: La Factoria
venues_mentioned.context: Amazing cocktails; wine bar & dance clubs

venues_mentioned.name: El Yunque rainforest
venues_mentioned.context: ~45 minutes from San Juan; hiking with waterfalls and viewpoints; Mount Britton Tower hike

venues_mentioned.name: Playa Las Golondrias + Cueva de las Golondrias
venues_mentioned.context: Sea urchin cave; crystal clear and very calm secondary beach

day_by_day_structure.theme: Old San Juan part 1 — forts, streets, and cocktails
Old San Juan part 2 — deeper exploration + Casita Miramar

notable_advice: Visit Castillo San Cristóbal first thing in the morning to avoid cruise ship crowds
Book accommodations well in advance
Make restaurant reservations ahead
Wear water shoes for rocky areas and El Yunque
Avoid Easter (many closures)
Avoid June-November (hurricane season)
